canonical_status.most_likely_intended_disease: Northern Leaf Blight (NLB), also called Northern Corn Leaf Blight or Turcicum Leaf Blight
canonical_status.reason: The Egypt-specific maize literature and disease databases identify the relevant disease as Northern Leaf Blight, not Northern Leaf Spot. NLS appears to be a non-standard name or a likely abbreviation error for NLB.
canonical_status.do_not_merge_warning: Do not label this as a confirmed separate NLS disease without a source defining NLS as a distinct pathogen-disease combination.

disease_name_for_record: Northern Leaf Blight (interpreted from requested NLS)

egypt_status.seasonal_pattern: Most often reported in late-summer or off-season maize in northern and north-western Delta areas.
egypt_status.egypt_environmental_context: Sprinkler irrigation in newly reclaimed areas can increase air moisture and disease incidence.
egypt_status.egypt_research_evidence: Egyptian breeding and field studies evaluated NLB resistance at Nubaria and Sakha and reported characteristic lesions and yield effects.

early_stage: Small oval, pale green, yellowish, or water-soaked spots
Early spots usually begin on lower leaves
characteristic_lesions: Long elliptical, spindle-shaped, or cigar-shaped lesions
Grey-green lesions that mature to grey, tan, or straw-brown
Lesions taper at the ends and run broadly parallel to leaf veins
Dark grey or olive fungal sporulation may be visible in humid weather, especially on lesion undersides
advanced_stage: Lesions enlarge and merge into irregular necrotic areas
Large parts of the leaf become brown, dry, and brittle
Whole leaves may wither and die
Severe upper-canopy infection can reduce grain filling and contribute to lodging

symptoms: pale green or yellow water-soaked spots

lesion_dimensions.typical_length_cm: Approximately 3–15 cm in Egyptian research; broader disease references report up to approximately 25–150 mm.
lesion_dimensions.note: Dimensions vary with cultivar, infection timing, weather, and disease severity.

distribution_on_plant: Usually starts on lower leaves and progresses upward; severe infections can affect most of the foliage.
affected_parts: upper canopy indirectly through photosynthetic loss
progression: Small pale or water-soaked spots appear on lower leaves.
Spots elongate into grey-green elliptical or cigar-shaped lesions.
Lesions mature to tan or straw-brown and may develop dark sporulation.
Lesions merge and destroy photosynthetic tissue.
Severe disease causes extensive leaf blighting, premature drying, reduced grain filling, and possible lodging.

environment.humidity: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness favour infection and sporulation.
environment.temperature: Approximately 18–27 °C is generally favourable for infection; Egyptian studies also associate disease with humid late-summer conditions.
environment.leaf_wetness: Dew, rainfall, and sprinkler irrigation increase infection risk.
environment.egypt_context: The northern and north-western Delta and sprinkler-irrigated newly reclaimed lands are important Egyptian risk contexts.

similar_diseases.name: Maydis Leaf Blight / Southern Leaf Blight
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Typically produces smaller tan or brown diamond-shaped or rectangular lesions rather than long cigar-shaped lesions.

similar_diseases.name: Gray Leaf Spot
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Usually produces narrow, sharply rectangular grey lesions restricted by veins.

similar_diseases.name: Common Rust
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Produces many raised orange-brown or black powdery pustules rather than large flat necrotic lesions.

research_notes: The principal data-quality issue is nomenclature: NLS was not found as the accepted name of a distinct maize disease in Egypt. The record preserves the user's requested label while explicitly mapping it to the documented Egyptian disease NLB.
